coaching.subject: acceptance criteria completeness and testability

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

evidence: 6 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Retarget generated config reference away from the hand-authored docs/config.md ADR to a separate generated companion (e.g. docs/config-reference.md), keeping docs/config.md untouched and byte-current drift applied only to the generated file.
evidence: Plan: 'Generate the config precedence/source/lifecycle reference in `docs/config.md` and a new indexed `docs/security.md`'
docs/config.md header: '# rebar configuration — design of record (ADR) + reference' / 'Status: **accepted**' — a hand-authored narrative, not a generated file

The realized generator scripts/gen_config_reference.py targets a SEPARATE docs/config-reference.md and states 'The hand-authored docs/config.md is left ENTIRELY untouched' — the sound approach the plan text contradicts
findings.finding: Step 4 directs generating the byte-current config precedence/source/lifecycle reference into docs/config.md, but that file is a hand-authored design-of-record ADR; generating into it (and enforcing byte-currency via a drift gate) would clobber the authored narrative or set generator and author in permanent conflict.
findings.location: Plan step 4 / Acceptance Criteria 'Generated config/security/operator docs are byte-current'
scenarios: A drift gate regenerates docs/config.md and overwrites the accepted ADR narrative
Author edits the ADR and the byte-current drift check immediately reddens the build
findings.suggested_fix: Change step 4 to generate into docs/config-reference.md (and docs/security.md), explicitly leaving the hand-authored docs/config.md ADR untouched; apply the byte-current drift gate only to the generated companions and update docs/README.md / docs/architecture.md navigation to point at them.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile parent AC4/step-4's 'ownership registry' data source with child 3199's explicit exclusion of it (either document owner/seam attribution in security.md or amend AC4 to name schema + deprecations + _ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES only).
evidence: Parent AC4: 'Generated config/security/operator docs are byte-current with schema/ownership registries...'
Parent plan step 4: 'from schema plus ownership/secret-name registries'
Child 3199 Outcome: 'There is no discrete "ownership registry" (ownership is a DERIVED AST classification in scripts/check_config_ownership.py); the generator does NOT read it.'
findings.finding: Parent plan step 4 and AC4 require the generated docs to be 'byte-current with schema/ownership registries', but the covering child (3199) explicitly disclaims any ownership-registry input ('There is no discrete ownership registry ... the generator does NOT read it').
scenarios: An operator/reviewer expects the generated security doc to reflect the approved owner→secret/seam mapping enumerated by the S7.1 ownership registry; the generator sources only schema + deprecations + _ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES, so any owner/seam attribution the epic wanted documented is not surfaced.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add an owner/seam-attribution section to docs/security.md derived from the S7.1 approved-owner registry, or amend parent AC4/step-4 to reference the secret-name inventory (_ADAPTER_SECRET_NAMES) rather than an 'ownership registry'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align parent plan step 4's named target (docs/config.md) with child 3199's decision to create docs/config-reference.md and leave config.md untouched.
evidence: Parent plan step 4: 'Generate the config precedence/source/lifecycle reference in docs/config.md and a new indexed docs/security.md'
Child 3199 Outcome: 'generates a NEW standalone, fully-generated docs/config-reference.md ... docs/config.md is LEFT ENTIRELY UNCHANGED'
findings.finding: Parent plan step 4 names docs/config.md as the generation target, but the covering child (3199) inverts this: it leaves docs/config.md entirely unchanged and generates a NEW docs/config-reference.md instead.
scenarios: A reviewer following the parent plan looks for the generated content in docs/config.md and finds it untouched; the machine-current reference lives in a differently-named file.
findings.suggested_fix: Update parent plan step 4 to name docs/config-reference.md (new generated file) instead of docs/config.md, matching the child's consumer-preserving decision.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve whether per-job SSM path removal is S7 scope (assign to a child) or already delivered by S6 (6f14) and remove the clause from parent AC7.
evidence: Parent AC7: 'Legacy facades, switches, per-job SSM path, ambient reloads, and migration exceptions are removed only after their proof passes'
Child 075b AC3: 'Legacy facades, switches, per-job ambient reloads, and migration exceptions are removed only after their proof passes' (no 'per-job SSM path')

Repo evidence that the per-job SSM path was already removed in RP-04 S6: src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py 'Instead of a per-job SSM fetch + process-global env patch (the old provisioned_signing_key)'; docs/adr/0098 §7 'The application removes REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM, SsmKeyFetcher, runtime boto3 ... and per-job provisioning.'
findings.finding: Parent AC7 requires removal of the 'per-job SSM path' among legacy paths, but the only covering sibling (075b AC3) omits that clause, enumerating 'per-job ambient reloads' instead; no other sibling covers per-job-SSM-path removal.
scenarios: If per-job SSM removal is still S7 work, it is owned by no child and would be left uncovered; if it was already completed in S6 (6f14), the parent AC7 clause is a residual reference that should be dropped to keep the completion metric honest.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the per-job SSM/REBAR_OPCERT_SSM_KEY_PARAM path was removed in S6 (6f14) and strike 'per-job SSM path' from parent AC7, or add an explicit per-job-SSM-removal item to child 075b's acceptance criteria.
